writeup: TIC 178354956 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.888565 days, identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry and pixel-level imaging. The primary eclipse produces a 6.67 percent dimming, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 71.6 in the periodogram analysis and confirmed at the pixel level with a peak signal-to-noise of 74.1. No secondary eclipse was detected. The target does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate. However, an important open question remains: the eclipse depths alternate significantly between odd and even cycles, which suggests the true orbital period may be double the initially measured value. Pixel-level confirmation and timing measurements support the corrected period of 2.888565 days reported here.
